docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Our Mission

Polyscope bridges pathology and data science for collaborative, AI-assisted image analysis.

docs.title: What?
docs.text: Polyscope is a web application for image sharing and annotation collection for digital pathology. Our aim is to connect our target users, pathologists, to data scientists, who are developing machine learning (ML) models for cancer diagnosis. In Polyscope, large whole-slide images can be explored in a web browser with fast response and a simplistic user interface. It supports single-cell annotations and tissue segmentation that we can collect to train ML models or visualize to validate the prediction of these models.

docs.title: Why?
docs.text:
Polyscope doesn't require installation or local storage at the users end. Polyscope can be accessed from almost all modern web browsers, including mobile devices. Polyscope supports a wide range of image formats. Sharing a view of a slide can be as easy as sharing a URL link. By using Polyscope, you have the chance to work with its developers, a team of data scientists and pathologists, and collaborate with them first-hand to form collobration and publish findings together, as opposed to developers of other software whom might not have the expertise in cancer research. Importantly, Polyscope further supports AI integration for AI-assisted pathology review and validation experience, with interactive controls for close-loop workflows.

Software Polyscope QuPath Halo (Indica Labs) No installation required ✅ ❌ ❌ Wide image format support ✅ ✅ ✅ Easy link sharing ✅ ❌ ✅ Mobile and tablet access ✅ ❌ ❌ Free for research ✅ ✅ ❌ AI integration ✅ ✅ ✅

docs.title: Learn More
docs.text: To learn more about the origins of Polyscope, and the developers and the support behind its development, see the About page.

docs.title: Developers
docs.text: Polyscope was originally developed by researchers in Dr. Yinyin Yuan's lab at The Institute of Cancer Research, London. After Dr. Yuan moved to The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center, we continue adding to its features at Yuan Lab. The current Polyscope version (GitHub Repository) is built upon the published version (GitHub repository) where Sebastian Schmittner was the main contributor. Current developers include Simon Castillo, Zhuohe Liu, Yasin Shokrollahi (ordered by last name). We are expanding Polyscope users from both within MD Anderson and outside collaborators, and we are happy to hear your feedback and requests.

docs.title: How to Contribute
docs.text:
You have the following options to report bugs, request features, or ask questions:

  • Send an email to the official support email address polyscope_admin@mdanderson.org.

  • Create an issue on the GitHub issue page.

You are also welcome to reach out to individual developers directly through their MD Anderson emails.

docs.title: Disclaimer
docs.text:
We are working with MD Anderson to ensure the safety and security of the data. User access are managed. However, as patient data are involved, we recommend checking with your institutions policy and compliance before uploading data to Polyscope. Deidentification is strongly recommended and please also consider if material transfer agreement (MTA) is needed. All data are stored in secure MD Anderson servers.

We are a non-profit organization. Despite that we are actively maintaining the software, we cannot guarantee the availability of the service. In addition, we will try to acknowledge all the issue reported and feature requested, but we cannot guarantee the timeline of the development. For urgent issues, please contact the developers directly. We are not responsible for any loss of data or any other damages caused by the use of this software.

This application is not approved for clinical use or primary diagnosis.

We are currently working to potentially open-source the application and accept external contributions. For now, please contact the developers if you want to contribute to the source code.

docs.title: AI Integration > Region Analysis
docs.text:
Abstract

Region analysis offers AI analysis of selected image regions of interest for cell segmentation.

docs.title: VitaminP-ResNet34 (H&E)
docs.text:
VitaminP-ResNet34 performs instance segmentation of cells. This model was trained on TBD dataset.

Model parameters:

  • Segmentation threshold: Default: 0.5. Range: 0.1-0.9. Meaning TBD.
  • Watershed threshold: Default: 0.3. Range: 0.1-0.8. Meaning TBD.
  • Min cell size (pixel): Default: 5. Range: 1-20. Meaning TBD.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
The AI-powered Region Analysis side panel holds configurations for region-of-interest (ROI) level real-time image analysis using built-in AI models.

To initiate analysis, following the steps below:

  1. Zoom the image view to a sufficiently small region, i.e. large magnification. Appropriate zoom levels are indicated by the Current Zoom Level block, which turns green when a appropriate zoom level is reached.
  2. Select a model from the AI Model dropdown and click the Start Analysis button to begin the analysis on the current view. This will fix the location and zoom of the image view. To move to another region, click the Stop button.
  3. Use the left mouse button and click and drag a rectangle ROI on the view. The selected ROI will be automatically send to the server to process.
  4. The result should typically be available in a couple of seconds. Once done, you will see statistics shown on the side panel, such as cell count and confidence.
  5. You may turn on overlay of the result or refine model parameters (see below).
  6. Click Clear Results to clean up previous analysis overlay from the current view.

To finetune the output, some models have associated parameters, which can be adjusted in the AI Parameter block. Click the Reprocess button to apply the changed parameters and obtain the updated results. Click the Reset button to revert to the default parameters.

To visualize the output, click the Show Results button and adjust display options in the Overlay Controls block:

  • Use the Opacity slider to set overlay opacity.
  • Use the Color picker to set overlay color. Note that filled cell area overlay use multiple colors and cannot be adjusted.
  • Toggle overlay visibility using the Show Overlays checkbox.
  • Toggle display type between cell boundries (single color) and filled area (multiple colors) using the Fill Cell Area checkbox.

Finally, the analysis results can be exported as a compressed folder (zip) by clicking the Export button. The zip file includes the cropped image of the selected ROI in full resolution along with associated overlay images. Source data for detected cell boundaries and instances are saved in a json file to support reproduction of the overlay in external programs. For more information, refer to the README.txt inside.

docs.title: Troubleshoot
docs.text:
Zoom to 80%+ for AI (crrently 4%).

Cause: region may be too large for analysis. Solution: Continue zooming in so that the selected regions will not have too many pixels.

Tip

If appropriate zoom level cannot be achieved even at the maximum zoom level, reduce the size of the browser window or use a higher page zoom from the browser control.

❌ Failed to Fetch

Cause: lost connection with AI server. Solution: Check internet connection. Contact support for more information.

docs.title: AI Integration > TME Tissue Segmentation
docs.text:
Abstract

Tumor microenvironment (TME) segmentation streamlines histology image analysis by identifying various tissue types to help quantify and understand tumor heterogeneity.

docs.title: SegFormer MIT-B3 (Lung)
docs.text:
SegFormer MIT-B3 (Lung) performs semantic segmentation. We used public annotations 1 to train Segformer 2 and DeepLabV3+ 3 models for TME segmentation. The training set included hematoxylin & eosin-stained (H&E) slides from breast and lung cancers in TCGA, combined with newly curated annotations from TCGA and four internal slides of surgically resected tumors, totaling 3403 patches (breast: 3110; lung: 293) at 0.44 μm/pixel. The models were trained to classify 10 tissue types: tumor, non-inflamed stroma, inflamed stroma, necrosis/hemorrhage, adipose tissue, bronchial epithelium, microvessel, foam-like macrophages, alveoli tissue, and muscle tissue. The performance of the model has been evaluated with pathological annotations (see reference).

Model parameters:

  • Patch size (pixel): Default: 512x512. Options: 256x256, 512x512, 896x896.
  • Scale Factor: Default: 1/16. Options: 1/32, 1/16, 1/8.
  • Apply Color Normalization: Default: false.

Model output:

A labeled image with colors denoting different tissue types.

Tissue colors
  • Non tissue, #000000 (Black)
  • Tumor, #8B0000 (Dark red/maroon)
  • Non-inflamed stroma, #FFFF00 (Yellow)
  • Inflamed stroma, #FF0000 (Red)
  • Necrosis/Hemorrhage, #FF00FF (Magenta)
  • Adipose tissue, #808000 (Olive/dark yellow)
  • Bronchial epithelium, #00FFFF (Cyan)
  • Microvessel, #0000FF (Blue)
  • Foam-like macrophages, #800080 (Purple/dark magenta)
  • Alveoli, #008000 (Green)
  • Muscle tissue, #000080 (Navy blue)

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
The TME Tissue Segmentation side panel holds configurations for TME Tissue Segmentation.

To initiate analysis, following the steps below:

  1. Select a model from the TME Model dropdown.
  2. Select appropriate options for model parameters.
  3. Click the Start TME Analysis button.
  4. The result should typically be available in a couple of minutes depends on the workload of the server and the size of the image. Once done, you will see statistics shown on the side panel below, such as tissue composition percentages.
  5. To show overlay of the result, click Show Results. The meaning of the overlay colors are displayed in the slide panel as well as mentioned above.
  6. Click Clear TME Results or Clear to delete analysis results.

The analysis results will be persistent even after the web page is closed.

To visualize the output,

  1. Click Remove to clean up previous analysis overlay from the current view. Note that this will only remove the display not the result. To re-enable overlay, click the Show Results again.
  2. You may toggle the overlay visbility using the Show/ Hide button.
  3. To adjust the display opacity, change the Opacity slider.

The analysis results can be exported as a compressed folder (zip) by clicking the Export button. The zip file includes the labeled image of the entire image region and a json file containing image metadata and analysis results.

Warning

The new analyis result will overwrite the old one if the old result was not cleared.

Info

Due to downsampling, when zoom-ed in, the boundries of the tissue regions might appear to be blury, which is normal.

docs.title: Pages > Image > Annotate Image
docs.text:
Abstract

Polyscope offers annotation on displayed images.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Click on the boxed regions in the screenshot below to learn more about each component:

docs.title: Annotation Controls
docs.text:
On the lower right of the slide view, you will find the following annotation control buttons:

  • Click and drag on the slide using left mouse button to add a rectangle annotation.
  • Click and drag on the slide using left mouse button to add an ellipse annotation.
  • Click ⟋ and drag on the slide using left mouse button to add a line segment annotation.
  • Click and drag on the slide using left mouse button to add an arrow annotation from tail to head.
  • Click to add a text annotation. In the popup window, type in the text after the prompt 'Please enter the annotation text'. Click 'OK' to add the annotation.
  • Click and drag on the slide using left mouse button to draw a freehand annotation.
  • Click . and left click on the slide to add a point annotation.
  • Click and click on the popup color swatches to change the annotation color.

Note that once an annotation is created, it cannot be edited (shape or color) unless it is deleted and recreated.

Tip

Annotations are automatically saved and you can safely close the browser window whenever you want.

docs.title: Delete Annotations
docs.text:
To delete an annotation, double click on it and click 'Yes' in the popup message box. Multiple annotations must be deleted one by one. For some annotation types such as points, it may be hard to double click on the annotation, so you can use the Annotations side panel to make selections before deletion.

Deletion cannot be undone by the user. However, deleted annotations are recorded and can be retrieved for later analysis if necessary.

docs.title: Annotation Statistics
docs.text:
In the Annotations section of the Analysis Tools side panel, you can view a real-time summary of created annotations. The statistics include counts for each annotation types, and a separate counts for each color.

Click on the annotatio type and color counts will apply attribute filter to the annotations, and filtered annotations will be shown in the list below. Click on the annotation entry in the list will center the selected annotation in the current view. Click the Delete Selected Annotation button to delete selected annotation.

Known issue

If annotation still apears after deletion, refresh the image page.

docs.title: Download Annotations
docs.text:
Annotations created in Polyscope can be exported to common formats such as CSV and JSON, as well as Polyscope TXT format. Click the Export button on the top right and select Annotations TXT menu option to download the annotations in Polyscope .txt format. Other formats follow similarly. Annotations can be downloaded at any time and multiple times if needed.

Important

Since the annotation file does not contain corresponding source image information, it is recommended to name the file properly with relevant information.

docs.title: TXT Annotation Format
docs.text:
We save the following properties of annotations, one row per annotations. The description of columns ordered from left to right are:

  • Annotation state: 0 = deleted, 1 = active.
  • Index: started from one, ordered by creation or deletion time.
  • Shape type: 0 = line segment, 1 = arrow, 2 = rectangle, 3 = ellipse, 4 = freehand, 5 = text, 6 = point.
  • Data, depending on the shape type:
  • Line segment, arrow: a list of 2 (x, y) coordinates denoting start and end points, e.g. [(0.1,0.2),(0.3,0.4)].
  • Rectangle, ellipse: a list of 2 (x, y) coordinates denoting the top-left and bottom-right corners, e.g. [(0.1,0.2),(0.3,0.4)].
  • Freehand: a list of (x, y) coordinates of variable length, e.g. [(0.1,0.2),(0.3,0.4),...].
  • Text: a list of a (x, y) coordinate and text string, e.g. [(0.1,0.2),'text'].
  • Point: a list of 2 (x, y) duplicated coordinates, marking the point location, e.g. [(0.1,0.2),(0.1,0.2)].
  • Note that coordinate values for both x and y axes are normalized to 0 to 1 according to the width of the slide.
  • Color: in hex such as #ffffff.
  • Created date and time: in the format of d/m/yyyy/HH:mm:ss in local time zone.

docs.title: CSV Annotation Format
docs.text:
CSV annotation file contains one annotation per row, with the following columns: ID, Type, TypeName, Color, Coordinates, Zoom, Date, Details. Fields follow similar defintion of the TXT format, with the following differences:

  • TypeName: a string denoting the shape name.
  • Details: a string contains simple properties of the annotation including width, height, and area in normalized units.

docs.title: JSON Annotation Format
docs.text: Polyscope uses GeoJSON schema for annotation export to a JSON file. JSON provides the most information rich way for saving annotations. In addition to annotation definitions, JSON format includes metadata such as export date, channel, annotation count. Many other software such as QuPath supports GeoJSON where you can import Polyscope created annotations.

docs.title: Pages > Index
docs.text:
Abstract

Index page offers a unified interface for file management, slide processing job submission, and status display, and it connects to result pages.

docs.title: Polyscope Storage
docs.text:
Polyscope offers dedicated file storage space for each user so they can upload files to be processed. Polyscope is not meant for permenant storage. Currently, there is no storage quota. We recommend following file management etiquettes below:

  • Processed files can be safetly deleted.
  • Perform routine clean up of old files to leave storage space for other users.
  • Refrain from using Polyscope as the primary data storage.
  • Follow consistent file naming conventions and folder organization.

For developer, user folder is located at /rsrch9/home/plm/polyscope/media/Users/.

docs.title: Files Tab
docs.text: Files Tab is the default view after logging in.

docs.title: Supported File Formats
docs.text:
Polyscope supported file formats include:

  • pathology slide formats (svs, ndpi, czi, scn, mrxs, vsi, vms);
  • medical imaging formats (dcm, nii, nrrd);
  • common image formats (jpg or jpeg, png, tif or tiff, bmp, gif, webp, jp2);
  • other formats (pdf).

Some tested file formats and their acquisition configuration are:

  • svs: Aperio/Leica scanner format at 20x/40x magnification. Pyramidal TIFF. RGB color space. Common for H&E, IHC, and other brightfield imaging.
  • ndpi: Hamamatsu NanoZoomer scanner format at 20x/40x magnification. Pyramidal structure with JPEG2000 compression. RGB color space. Standard for H&E and special stains.
  • scn: Leica SCN format from Aperio AT/AT2 scanners. Pyramidal TIFF. RGB color space. Common for clinical pathology slides.
  • ome.tiff: Support of OME TIFF may be limited to single channel.

docs.title: Upload Files
docs.text:
Viewing slides on Polyscope starts with file uploading. Multiple files can be uploaded concurrently, with a combined maximum file size limit of 5 GB.

To upload files, you can:

  1. click the Upload Files button;
  2. drag files to the file drop area on the page;
  3. click anywhere on the file drop area.

A progress bar will be displayed on top of the page for all files being uploaded.

Tip

When a file is uploading, you cannot upload a new file. However, you can select multiple files to be uploaded at the same time.

Note

File and folder names only support valid characters of letters (a-z, A-Z), numerals (0-9), underscore (_) and period (.). Underscores will be used in place of unsupporting characters such as space () or brackets.

Warning

Do NOT close the browser tab/window or refresh the page while uploading, otherwise uploading will be disrupted and you need to initiate new uploading.

docs.title: Manage Files
docs.text:
After files are uploaded, you can perform file management operations.

  • Create a new folder: click the New Folder button.

  • Rename a file or a folder: click on the (pen) icon when hovering on the file or folder. Alternatively, select the file or folder through the checkbox and click the Rename button or press F2. Type the new name in the text box.

  • Delete file(s) or folders: select the file(s) and/or folder(s) using the checkboxes and click the Delete button. A popup dialog will shown to confirm the deletion action.

    Warning

    File deletion cannot be undone by user. However, in rare cases, please contact us for file recovery.

  • Move a file into a folder: click and drag the file to the folder.

Currently, duplicating file or folder, moving folder(s) or multiple files, and moving a file outside a folder is not supported.

docs.title: Process Files
docs.text: Uploaded files of various formats need to be converted to internal and standardized format (Deep Zoom File, DZI) so Polyscope can offer easy and responsive access to the images through a web browser. To process uploaded files, select the file(s) using the checkboxes and click the Process button. Currently, batch process files by selecting a folder is not supported but you can navigate into the folder to select all/multiple files within. A job will be created for each file to parse and convert the image format. The page will automatically transition to the Processing Tab once a processing job is submitted.

docs.title: Processing Tab
docs.text: The Processing Tab displays the queue of jobs to be processed and their status. You will see the job status going from checksum, pending, upload, queue, processing, all the way to finished. Normally, processing of a file takes somewhere around 1 to 10 minumtes. As all users share the same processing queue, during peak usage or batch submission of many jobs, jobs may be queued. After the job is finished, "finished" status will be displayed, and click view results button to go to the processed image. Otherwise, navigate to My Results to view the processed files.

docs.title: Pages > Login
docs.text:
Abstract

Login page grants user access to Polyscope, with support for MD Anderson Cancer Center single sign-on (SSO).

Polyscope is accessible both within and outside MD Anderson Cancer Center. While Polyscope is hosted on secure servers within MD Anderson Cancer Center, VPN connection is not necessary to access Polyscope outside the internal network. Polyscope supports most modern broswers, including Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge.

docs.title: Sign In
docs.text:
The login page is the gateway to the Polyscope application when users first visit the site at https://polyscope.mdanderson.org/. Logging in is required except to view the documentation and viewing shared Polyzoomer pages.

To log in, enter your MD Anderson username and password and click Sign In. After successful log-in, you will be redirected to the Index page.

Tip

You will be automatically logged out after 45 minutes of inactivity.

docs.title: Sign Out
docs.text: To sign out from Polyscope, click the avatar button on the top right of the Index page showing your username. Click on the popup menu Sign Out to sign out.

docs.title: Pages > My Results
docs.text:
Abstract

My Results page is the place to manage all processed images and create image views.

From the Index page, click the My Results button in the navigation bar to go to the My Results page. You have access only to your own user directory under https://polyscope.mdanderson.org/customers/<your_email> where <your_email> is your email address/username where @ and . is replaced by -.

Example

For jsmith1@mdanderson.org, the user page is located at https://polyscope.mdanderson.org/customers/jsmith1-mdanderson-org/.

docs.title: File List Side Panel
docs.text:
Use the buttons to the left to organize the processed files.

  • : delete selected file(s);
  • : create a new folder;
  • : sort file list;
  • : To be removed;
  • : create Multizoomer from multiple images.

To move file(s) to a folder, either drag the selected files to the destination folder, or use context menu of the image thumbnails to 'copy' or 'cut' and then 'paste'.

Operations like deletion and Multizoomer creation requires selection of multiple files: click on the image thumbnail to select, which will highlight the selection in yellow; click again to deselect.

Finally, the slider allows you to adjust the thumbnail size.

Currently, file name renaming of processed files and their folders is not supported.

Known issue

Although offered as an option, a folder cannot be deleted.

Double click on the thumbnail of an image to view it in the Image Page.

docs.title: Create Multizoomer Image View
docs.text:
Multiple images can be linked to create one Multizoomer page. In a Multizoomer view, the display areas of each file are synchronized across user's pan and zoom actions. Before creating Multi-view pages, individual images need to be processed first.

To create a Multizoomer view, following the steps below:

  1. Drag one or more processed images from the left side panel to the right side of the My Results page. Images can be arranged in a grid pattern.
  2. You may click the button to remove added images on the right side.
  3. Optionally, click the button to set the reference image (see Synchronized view). If not selected, the first image will be the reference.
  4. When all files are added, click the button on the left to create the view.

After a couple of seconds, a Multizoomer image page will be created and added to the list of files on the left. Double click on the thumbnail of an image to view it in the Image Page.

Note

Changes (annotation edits) to the underlying polyzoomer files will propogate to the dependent Multizoomer views.

docs.title: Synchronized View
docs.text:
Once a Multizoomer is created, interactions are synchronized based on the reference image:

  • Pan and zoom movements applied to the reference image will be mirrored across all other image(s) in the Multizoomer.
  • Other operations will function as they do on an individual image.

docs.title: Pages > Image > View Image
docs.text:
Abstract

This page details controls and functions when viewing images on the Image page.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Click on the boxed regions in the screenshot below to learn more about each component:

docs.title: View Modes
docs.text:
The goal of the Image Page is to let users view and annotate images. This page can be configured to two modes:

  • Polyzoomer: referring to a single image view.
  • Multizoomer: referring to a combination of multiple image views.

Before you start, make sure you choose a set of annotation shapes and colors to be used for each semenatic class to ensure consistency. Once an annotation is created, it cannot be edited (shape or color) unless it is deleted and recreated.

docs.title: View Toolbar
docs.text:
You can control the displayed image view by mouse or keyboard. On the top left of the image view, you will find the following view control buttons:

  • Click or or use mouse scroll to zoom. Double left click to zoom in.
  • Drag with left mouse button to pan.
  • Click to reset the view.
  • Click to display the current image in full screen.
  • Click or icons to rotate the image 90 degrees clockwise or counterclockwise, respectively.

In addition, keyboard offers the following alternative view controls:

  • Press = or - to zoom in and out, respectively.
  • Press Up, Down, Left, Right or W, A, S, D keys to pan.
  • Press 0 to reset the view.

docs.title: Image Controls
docs.text: To adjust the displayed image brightness, contrast, and saturation, using the sliders on the Analysis Tools side panel. Click the Reset button to reset the properties.

docs.title: Navigator
docs.text: The navigator is at the top right corner of the image view. The navigator enables quick random jumping to locations on the image, by clicking on the corresponding locations on the displayed thumbnail in the navigator.

docs.title: Download View (Screenshot)
docs.text:
Polyscope image page supports multiple formats and contents of screenshot export. Options can be accessed throught the Screenshot button on the top right of the page.

  • Entire webpage area: Select Full Page capture area;
  • Viewer area: Select Viewer Only (UI components will be excluded);
  • Cropped viewer area: Select Select Region.

Next, select the file format from the Format dropdown menu PNG, JPEG, WebP. PNG is recommended for the best quality. For JPEG or WebP format, you can make trade-off between file size and image quality by adjusting the Quality slider, where 100% means best image quality which requires the largest file size.

Finally, click the Take Screenshot button and save the screenshot using the popup file saving dialog.

Alternatively, right click over the image area and select the Save image As... context menu option. Supported file formats is png. This option is a shortcut for viewer area screenshot.

docs.title: Copy View
docs.text: You can also copy the content of the current viewing area to the clip board by selecting the Copy Image menu option in the right click context menu.

docs.title: Link Sharing
docs.text:
You can share the Polyscope image pages with others for collaboration through URL links. The URL can link to the image or include the current viewing area of the image.

The Share button on the top right offers convenient sharing options.

A Polyzoomer/Multizoomer link might look like this: 

https://polyscope.mdanderson.org/customers/jsmith1-mdanderson-org/Path000001_202402061731/page/test001/index.html?slide=slide1_UNKNOWNCHANNEL0001&patient=test001&channel=_UNKNOWNCHANNEL0001&x=0.5000&y=0.5714&z=0.6286
  • To share the page with default view, use the truncated URL https://polyscope.mdanderson.org/customers/jsmith1-mdanderson-org/Path000001_202402061731/page/test001 (you may omit the index.html part);
  • To share the current viewing area, use the entire URL which includes queries after ?.

Warning

The link is publicly accessible, so it is advisable to keep it confidential.

Tip

If you need to share an image with multiple independent users, consider creating multiple Polyzoomers/Multizoomers from the same file.

docs.title: Tutorial 1: Login, Navigate, Create Polyzoomer
docs.text:
Abstract

This tutorial serves as a quick guide for Polyscope from logging in and uploading files to viewing images.

docs.title: Login to Polyscope
docs.text: Access Polyscope at (https://polyscope.mdanderson.org/, which is accessible both within and outside MD Anderson. To log in, enter your MD Anderson username and password at the Login Page.

docs.title: Navigate Folders and Upload/Copy Data
docs.text: Then, select image files to upload. Make sure files are within size limit and file formats are supported. Multiple files can be uploaded concurrently. After successfull uploading, you can organize files e.g. rename, delete, or create folders.

docs.title: Create Polyzoomer from File
docs.text:
A Polyzoomer is an interactive view of an uploaded image, which must be created before viewing. Ensure that file names are properly formatted and that PHI is removed before proceeding. Select one or more files and click the Process to DZI button to submit files to be processed.

Processing takes approximately 1 to 10 minutes, which you can check the progress at the Processing Tab. Once a Polyzoomer is created, the original source files can be deleted.

docs.title: My Results Page and Open Polyzoomer
docs.text:
The My Results page lists all processed images for each user. Simple organization can be done on processed images like source files. Double click on the thumbnail to open a Polyzoomer.

It is also possible to create a Multizoomer from multiple Polyzoomers, enabling multi-view interaction (see Tutorial 3).

docs.title: Explore Polyzoomer
docs.text:
A Polyzoomer page provides an interactive view of an image. You can use the mouse and the keyboard to explore the images at different locations and zoom levels. The side panel provides additional image adjustment.

Annotations can be created, viewed, and downloaded directly within Polyzoomer (see Tutorial 2).

docs.title: Share Polyzoomer
docs.text: A URL link can be generated for sharing the Polyzoomer page. Before sharing, double-check that image file names are properly formatted and PHI is removed. The link is accessible to everyone, so keep it confidential.

docs.title: Tutorial 3: Create and View a Multizoomer
docs.text:
Abstract

This tutorial covers the creation and viewing of a Multizoomer, synchronized viewing of multiple image views.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Multizoomer is a powerful tool that enables synchronized viewing of multiple images. It is particularly useful for:

  • Displaying image annotations from multiple sources.
  • Viewing multiple imaging channels simultaneously.
  • Comparing different imaging modalities of adjacent tissue.
  • Visualizing AI model outputs alongside original images.

A Multizoomer is composed of multiple Polyzoomers. Importantly, it does not duplicate the underlying Polyzoomers; this means that any annotation changes propagate bidirectionally, ensuring data consistency. However, if a Polyzoomer is deleted, a blank view will appear in its place within the Multizoomer.

docs.title: Creating a Multizoomer
docs.text:
To create a Multizoomer, follow these steps:

  1. Drag individual Polyzoomers onto the right side of the interface to configure the Multizoomer layout.
  2. It is recommended to use a maximum of two columns for better organization.
  3. While the system supports an unlimited number of views, keeping it to around six views ensures clarity and usability.
  4. Click the Create Multizoomer button to finalize the layout. This action will navigate to the newly created Multizoomer page.
  5. Click the α (alpha) button to designate one Polyzoomer as the reference Polyzoomer. The reference Polyzoomer controls synchronized actions across all views (explained in the next section).

docs.title: Multizoomer Interaction
docs.text:
Once a Multizoomer is created, interactions are synchronized based on the reference Polyzoomer:

  • Pan and zoom movements applied to the reference Polyzoomer will be mirrored across all other Polyzoomers in the Multizoomer.
  • Other operations will function as they do on an individual Polyzoomer.

docs.title: Sharing a Multizoomer
docs.text:
Sharing a Multizoomer is straightforward:

  • The URL of the Multizoomer page serves as the shareable link. Example: https://polyscope.mdanderson.org/customers/jsmith1-mdanderson-org/multizooms/Path000009_202502041751/page/INDEX/
  • The link is publicly accessible, so it is advisable to keep it confidential.
  • It can be accessed both inside and outside MD Anderson without requiring a VPN.
  • Since a Multizoomer depends on its source Polyzoomers, consider creating multiple Polyzoomers from a single image if you need to share them with different individuals independently.

By following these steps, you can efficiently create, interact with, and share Multizoomers for various imaging and annotation tasks.

docs.title: Tutorial 2: Annotate using Polyscope
docs.text:
Abstract

This tutorial explains how to create and view a Polyzoomer, a single image view, and how to annotate images using Polyscope.

docs.title: Access Polyscope Polyzoomer Page
docs.text:
The URL of a Polyzoomer page serves as its shareable link, for example: https://polyscope.mdanderson.org/customers/jsmith1-mdanderson-org/Path000010_202502182331/page/test001/. This link is accessible to everyone, so it is important to keep it confidential.

Polyscope is available both within and outside MD Anderson without the need for a VPN. A desktop browser is recommended for the best experience, but mobile devices with touchscreens are also supported. While co-editing is possible, it is recommended to use only one tab per link to avoid conflicts.

docs.title: Create Annotations and Their Types
docs.text:
Before starting an annotation task, consult the annotation requester to determine the appropriate annotation type. Since Polyscope does not save color code descriptions, it is advised to record the color coding before beginning annotation work.

To set a color, click the tool. Click on an annotation type icon to enter annotation mode; clicking the icon again will exit this mode. Popular annotation types are:

  • . Point annotation: Each left-click creates one annotation.
  • Freehand drawing: Left-click and drag to draw.
  • Rectangle annotation: Left-click to define one corner, then drag and release to set the opposite corner.

The color can be changed during annotation mode.

docs.title: Edit and Delete Annotations
docs.text: Annotations cannot be moved or resized after creation. If changes are needed, the annotation must be deleted and recreated. To delete an annotation, click on it and follow the prompt. Multiple annotations must be deleted one by one.

docs.title: Review Annotations
docs.text:
You can use the mouse and the keyboard to explore the images at different locations and zoom levels to review annotations. Here are the common interactions:

  • Pan: Mouse left click to drag or press Up, Down, Left, or Right keys.
  • Zoom: Use the mouse scroll wheel or press = or - keys.
  • Full screen: Click to enter full screen view.

Annotation statistics are displayed in the side panel. Annotations should refresh automatically, but if they do not, try refreshing the page or reopening the tab.

docs.title: Download Annotations
docs.text:
Click the Export button to save annotations in CSV, JSON, or TXT format.

Since the annotation file does not contain corresponding slide information, it is recommended to rename the file immediately after downloading. Annotations can be downloaded at any time and multiple times if needed.
